"50X The Cash" is close to selling out, with only a small slice of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Everything above about "50X The Cash" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
981.headline: Early stage or late

985.body:
The most common win left on "MAX-A-MILLION" is $30. The second biggest prize left is $100,000, and six of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Tomorrow's count on "MAX-A-MILLION" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
985.headline: What the prize table shows

988.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Emerald 10's", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is in the second half of its run, with two of five top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything here about "Emerald 10's" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 8.
988.headline: How far along this game is

990.headline: What the prize table shows

992.body:
The most common win left on "$2 MILLION VAULT" is $20. The second biggest prize left is $100,000, and one of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Every line of $2 MILLION VAULT's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
992.headline: What's actually left to win

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has three of six top prizes left and is in the second half of its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

Tomorrow's count on "$5,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
993.headline: How much has sold

994.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$25,000 Triple Play" have been sold. The game is well into its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

The numbers for "$25,000 Triple Play" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.

995.headline: What the prize table shows

996.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with four of five still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
996.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain
